topic: Heinz redesigned the ketchup bottle to sit upside down so kids could squeeze it
title: Heinz Turned Its Bottle Upside Down. Sales Jumped.
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script: Every meal, the same struggle. Tapping the Heinz ketchup bottle. Shaking it. Waiting for the thick sauce to finally move. It was a universal annoyance. Heinz, a brand known for its classic glass bottles, had a problem. Customer frustration. But instead of a new formula, they chose a physical redesign. They turned the bottle upside down. The cap became the base. Gravity did the work. Ketchup was always at the opening, ready to pour. This wasn't just a convenience upgrade. It was a clever business move. Immediately, sales saw a significant boost. Some reports claimed double-digit growth in specific markets. The simple act of fixing one common, annoying user experience translated directly into increased revenue. It showed that sometimes, the biggest business trick isn't a complex strategy. It's understanding a basic customer pain point and solving it with elegant simplicity. Heinz didn't just sell ketchup. They sold convenience. And customers paid for it. This is a classic example of a sneaky deal: identify friction, eliminate it, and watch your bottom line grow.
